item.title: Essex at 7, Tuesday 10 November: Russell Brand, who grew up in Grays, could challenge his 10-and-a-half-year rape sentence, solicitor tells the Standard
item.description: The Seax morning briefing for Tuesday 10 November.
item.content:encoded:
Weather

Cloudy, high 10°C, low 8°C, 40% chance of rain.

The stories that matter

Russell Brand, who grew up in Grays, could challenge his 10-and-a-half-year rape sentence, solicitor tells the Standard

Grays · A criminal defence solicitor not involved in the case told the Evening Standard an appeal against the sentence was the most likely next step, after the comedian was jailed at Southwark Crown Court on Monday.

Police still seeking witnesses to Sunday's early-hours crash that killed two people on Chelmsford's Copperfield Road

Chelmsford · Essex Police wants doorbell, dashcam and eyewitness accounts after a driver and passenger died when their Ford Fiesta struck a property wall near Havisham Way.

Southend's fenced-off Three Shells Lagoon should be removed and the beach restored, council report says

Southend-on-Sea · Southend-on-Sea City Council says taking out the failed lagoon is its preferred long-term option, and the proposal goes to Cabinet on 16 November.

Braintree and County Hall leaders vow to resist Home Office bid to keep Wethersfield asylum site open after April 2027

Wethersfield, Braintree · The government has applied to extend its use of the former airbase near Braintree, where asylum seekers have been housed since July 2023, and both councils say they will look at ways to oppose it.

Harlow college shut over building safety fears wins approval for a permanent new school

Harlow · Sir Frederick Gibberd College pupils have been taught in temporary classrooms for two years after the modular main building was closed.

Maldon council says national rules leave little room to refuse new homes in Tollesbury, Great Totham and Latchingdon

Maldon, Tollesbury, Great Totham, Latchingdon · The district's leader says unpopular village schemes cannot be turned down without sound planning evidence, as a new national scheme also takes many decisions away from committee.

Multi-agency raids on more than 100 Essex premises seize £10,360 in cash and illicit cigarettes

Essex · Operation Machinize, coordinated by the National Crime Agency and carried out locally by Essex Police with partner agencies, targeted organised crime linked to businesses across the county.

Southend council still heading for a £12m overspend as one child's care placement tops £1m a year

Southend-on-Sea · The latest six-month forecast shows the gap narrowing by about £1.3m, but children's social care costs have climbed by around £1.5m since the summer.

From Council Watch

Government direction pushes Southend's draft local plan towards a six-week public consultation

Southend-on-Sea City Council · The new plan would set the rules for where homes go and how the council handles applications for shared houses, affordable housing and hot food takeaways.

Southend aims to bring council home repairs up to industry norms by Christmas after regulator judgement

Southend-on-Sea City Council · Electrical safety checks on council homes are now close to complete, but councillors heard that repairs remain the weak spot in Southend's response to the social housing regulator.

Three in four Thurrock children entering care now get their first health check on time, up from 36%

Thurrock Council · Councillors scrutinising children's services heard that initial health assessments within the 20-day legal deadline have more than doubled.

Travel

  • Basildon: Pipps Hill Road North and Hardings Elm Road closed between Oak Road and the A127 from Mon 9 Nov for about 26 days for gas mains work; diversion via A127, A132, A129 and A176
  • c2c: no trains at Dagenham Dock, Rainham or Purfleet until at least end of Tue 10 Nov; shuttle buses Upminster to Grays about every 30 min, extra Pitsea to Grays buses 06:50 to 09:30
  • 14 to 15 Nov: buses replace trains Sudbury to Marks Tey; Sunday also Ipswich to Colchester and Manningtree to Harwich
  • 21 to 22 Nov: no trains Braintree to Witham; Sunday also Colchester to Ingatestone

Results

  • Chelmsford City 2-2 Ebbsfleet United (National League South)
  • Cardiff Fire 3-9 Chelmsford Chieftains (NIHL South Division 1)

On today

  • Milo Edwards: Catamaran, Colchester
  • The Proclaimers, Westcliff-on-Sea

Every story links to the original reporting. More all day at theseax.com.

item.title: Essex at 7, Monday 9 November: Colchester A12 death: witnesses sought after young man is struck near junction 26 on Saturday evening
item.description: The Seax morning briefing for Monday 9 November.
item.content:encoded:
Weather

Mist clearing to sunny intervals, high 10°C, low 4°C, 5% chance of rain.

⚠ Met Office yellow warning for fog in force until 11am Monday 9 November

The stories that matter

Colchester A12 death: witnesses sought after young man is struck near junction 26 on Saturday evening

Colchester · The collision near junction 26 shortly before 5.30pm on Saturday closed both carriageways until shortly before 5am on Sunday.

Mist and fog greet Essex commuters on Monday with Met Office warning in force until 11am

Essex · Visibility is poor for the start of the week, with mist reported in Chelmsford early on Monday before sunny intervals are forecast to take over.

Grays-raised Russell Brand due before Southwark Crown Court judge for sentencing today

Grays · The Thurrock-born comedian was convicted of rape and three sexual assaults against four women between 2004 and 2009, and has been in custody since the verdicts.

Man in his 20s killed as his car hits a parked vehicle in Harlow crash at Kingsland

Harlow · Police are asking for dash cam and doorbell footage after the early Sunday collision near Tendring Road, which kept the road shut for several hours.

Historian wants Grays church memorial naming 22 boys lost in 1875 Goliath training ship fire

Grays · Local researcher Peter Valentine says he has traced the names of the workhouse boys and believes they lie in an unmarked grave at St Peter and St Paul's Church.

Peter Swift wins World Sausage Throwing Championship on Harwich Green for third year running

Harwich · The 29-year-old hurled an out-of-date banger 148.5ft to keep his title at the quirky contest run by Tendring Camra, while a Great Bromley butcher took the Champion Sausage of Tendring prize.

From Council Watch

Southend aims to bring council home repairs up to industry norms by Christmas after regulator judgement

Southend-on-Sea City Council · Electrical safety checks on council homes are now close to complete, but councillors heard that repairs remain the weak spot in Southend's response to the social housing regulator.

Three in four Thurrock children entering care now get their first health check on time, up from 36%

Thurrock Council · Councillors scrutinising children's services heard that initial health assessments within the 20-day legal deadline have more than doubled.

Epping Forest councillors asked to back raising the top fly-tipping fine from £1,000 to £5,000

Epping Forest District Council · A motion to full council called for the district's maximum fixed penalty for fly-tipping to rise fivefold now that the law allows it.

Travel

  • A130 southbound between Howe Green Interchange and Rayleigh Spur: weekend closure due to end about 6am Mon 9 Nov; diversion via A12 and A127 until it lifts
  • c2c: no trains at Dagenham Dock, Rainham or Purfleet until at least end of Tue 10 Nov; shuttle buses Upminster to Grays about every 30 min, extra Pitsea to Grays buses 06:50 to 09:30
  • 14 to 15 Nov: buses replace trains Sudbury to Marks Tey; Sunday also Ipswich to Colchester and Manningtree to Harwich
  • 21 to 22 Nov: no trains Braintree to Witham; Sunday also Colchester to Ingatestone

Results

  • Swindon Wildcats 2 6-5 Chelmsford Chieftains (NIHL National)
  • Colchester United 1-0 Worcester City (FA Cup first round)
  • Chelmsford City 2-1 Farnborough (National League South)
  • Dagenham & Redbridge 2-2 Billericay Town (National League South)
  • Weston-super-Mare 4-1 Braintree Town (National League South)
  • Bowers & Pitsea 0-3 Buckhurst Hill (Isthmian North)
  • Brightlingsea Regent 0-0 Fakenham Town (Isthmian North)
  • Little Oakley 0-1 Walthamstow (Isthmian North)

On today

  • Tony Hadley: The Christmas Big Band Tour, Westcliff-on-Sea · £48
  • The Other Side, Westcliff-on-Sea
  • Larry Dean: Hellbent, Chelmsford
  • The Other Side Of Murder, Westcliff-on-Sea

Every story links to the original reporting. More all day at theseax.com.

item.title: Essex at 7, Sunday 8 November: Essex falls silent for Remembrance Sunday as parades close town centres from Colchester to Leigh-on-Sea
item.description: The Seax morning briefing for Sunday 8 November.
item.content:encoded:
Weather

Mist, high 10°C, low 2°C, 10% chance of rain.

The stories that matter

Essex falls silent for Remembrance Sunday as parades close town centres from Colchester to Leigh-on-Sea

Chelmsford, Colchester, Brentwood, Saffron Walden · Services at war memorials across the county mark the 11am two-minute silence today, with First Essex changing buses in 16 towns and villages while roads are closed for parades.

A12 shut between Colchester junctions 26 and 28 after car hits pedestrian, with diversions through the town

Colchester · Police and ambulance crews were called to the A12 at Colchester on Saturday evening, and National Highways said the road was expected to stay closed through the evening.

Dash cam appeal as police link three pre-dawn Tilbury incidents involving men falsely claiming to be officers

Tilbury · Officers believe the incidents near St Chads Road and Calcutta Road between 4am and 4.45am on Saturday are connected, and say genuine police can always show a warrant card.

Essex commissioner brands regional 'mega force' plan not fit for purpose as merger review awaits publication

Essex · Roger Hirst told the BBC there is no evidence bigger forces perform better, a day after the Met chief called for the 43 forces in England and Wales to shrink to as few as eight.

Essex drivers warned before Christmas crackdown as drug-driving arrests reach 1,960 in ten months

Essex · Roads policing officers held more than twice as many people on suspicion of drug-driving as drink-driving between January and October, and the force is now planning its festive campaign.

South Basildon MP James McMurdock raises alarm over how few refused asylum claims end in returns

Basildon, Thurrock · Home Office figures show only around one in ten asylum claims refused from 2025 has so far led to a recorded return, and the MP for South Basildon and East Thurrock wants the Government to publish clearer data.

Parking at Princess Alexandra Hospital in Harlow to cost more from 17 November

Harlow · The trust says the rise is a small inflation-linked increase, with the first 20 minutes staying free and existing exemptions kept.

E-bike pods at Harwich station and on the harbour ferry aim to keep coastal visitors moving

Harwich · Greater Anglia and Freeport East have launched the Harwich Haven Eezybike Connect network, with five pods at stations and on the Harwich Harbour Ferry.

From Council Watch

Tendring budgets for life beyond 2028 as the government pauses the council shake-up

Tendring District Council · With Whitehall reviewing its plan to replace Essex's councils, Tendring's cabinet has agreed to plan four years ahead, and backed money for toilets, playgrounds and housing staff.

Thurrock's special needs funding gap keeps growing as Treetops School plans 110 more places

Thurrock Council · Children's services are on course to underspend by about £0.5m, but the grant that pays for special educational needs is heading deeper into deficit, councillors heard.

Thurrock picked as one of seven national pilots helping children stay with their wider family

Thurrock Council · The Kinship Zones pilot will give practical, emotional and financial support to relatives raising children, as Thurrock reshapes its children's social care.

Travel

  • A12 near Colchester: closed in both directions after a serious crash on Saturday evening, with the closure expected through the night; avoid the area
  • Sun 8 Nov: First buses diverted for Remembrance in 16 places; Chelmsford bus station closed 10am to 12.30pm (board at Coval Lane, Retail Market or Parkway), Colchester Head St and High St shut 8am to 1.30pm
  • A12 near Chelmsford: crash reported this afternoon causing severe delays; check before you travel
  • A130 southbound closed between Howe Green Interchange and Rayleigh Spur from 8pm Fri 6 Nov to about 6am Mon 9 Nov; diversion via A12 and A127 at Gallows Corner

Results

  • Swindon Wildcats 2 6-5 Chelmsford Chieftains (NIHL National)
  • Colchester United 1-0 Worcester City (FA Cup first round)
  • Chelmsford City 2-1 Farnborough (National League South)

On today

  • Barleylands Family Fireworks, Barleylands, Billericay
  • Essex Christmas Fair, Cressing Temple Barns, Cressing, near Braintree · Adults £7, concessions £6, under-18s free
  • Chelmsford Hockey Club Beer Festival, Sports Pavilion, Chelmer Park, Beehive Lane, Galleywood · Free entry
  • Cammas Hall Farm Fireworks and Bonfire Night, Cammas Hall Farm, Hatfield Broad Oak
  • Castle Point Remembrance Sunday services, South Benfleet, Canvey Island, Hadleigh and Thundersley · Free

Every story links to the original reporting. More all day at theseax.com.

item.title: Essex at 7, Saturday 7 November: A130 southbound stays shut all weekend between Howe Green and the Rayleigh Spur
item.description: The Seax morning briefing for Saturday 7 November.
item.content:encoded:
Weather

Sunny intervals after early fog, high 11°C, low 5°C, 10% chance of rain.

⚠ Met Office yellow warning for fog in force until 11am Saturday 7 November

The stories that matter

A130 southbound stays shut all weekend between Howe Green and the Rayleigh Spur

Howe Green & Rayleigh · Drivers heading south from Chelmsford towards Basildon and Southend face a signed diversion via the A12 and A127 until about 6am on Monday, with fog adding to the delays on Saturday morning.

Met chief's call for just eight to ten forces sharpens fight over Essex Police's future

Essex · Sir Mark Rowley says the 43 forces in England and Wales should shrink to as few as eight, as Essex commissioner Roger Hirst insists the county wants to keep its own force.

Plans emerge for 1GW solar and battery energy park on the Dengie Peninsula

Bradwell-on-Sea, Dengie & Burnham-on-Crouch · Developer Low Carbon has started the national planning process for a scheme it says could power 250,000 homes, and Maldon District Council has until 24 November to say what studies it needs.

Southend opens final consultation on Local Plan it was ordered to publish by ministers

Southend-on-Sea · Residents have until 21 December to comment on the draft blueprint for homes, jobs and infrastructure, which the city council published only after the housing minister intervened.

Essex County Council asks residents to help close a £170m gap in one of its toughest budgets this century

Chelmsford · The county council has opened a month-long consultation on its 2027/28 budget, saying government funding changes will cost it more than £50m a year.

Thurrock's baby death rate is 37% above the national average, new health strategy warns

Grays & Thurrock · A draft Health and Wellbeing Strategy for 2027 to 2030 puts pregnancy and the early years at the centre of plans to give Thurrock babies a healthier start.

Basildon councillors refuse 910-home Foots Farm scheme near Billericay's Sun Corner

Billericay · The planning committee turned down the green belt application off Southend Road, but the developers' appeal is already heading to a public inquiry next May.

More than 50,000 still waiting at Southend Hospital as trust backlog falls by 14,000

Southend-on-Sea · Hospital chief executive Fiona Ryan told councillors there is still a long way to go, although waiting lists across the Mid and South Essex trust are starting to come down.

Travel

  • Fog: Met Office yellow warning until 11am Saturday. Allow extra time and use dipped headlights
  • A130 southbound closed between Howe Green Interchange and Rayleigh Spur from 8pm Fri 6 Nov to about 6am Mon 9 Nov; diversion via A12 and A127 at Gallows Corner
  • c2c: no trains at Dagenham Dock, Rainham or Purfleet until at least end of Tue 10 Nov; shuttle buses Upminster to Grays about every 30 min, extra Pitsea to Grays buses 06:50 to 09:30
  • A12 southbound closed overnight between J25 Marks Tey and Hatfield Peverel for three nights from Wed 4 Nov, 9pm to 5am; diversion via A120 and A131

On today

  • Barleylands Family Fireworks, Barleylands, Billericay
  • Orsett Showground Bonfire Night (30th year), Orsett Showground, Rectory Road, Orsett · £9.50, under-5s £2.50, OAPs free, pay on the gate
  • Essex Christmas Fair, Cressing Temple Barns, Cressing, near Braintree · Adults £7, concessions £6, under-18s free
  • Chelmsford Hockey Club Beer Festival, Sports Pavilion, Chelmer Park, Beehive Lane, Galleywood · Free entry
  • Fabulous Fungi Walk, Belfairs Nature Discovery Centre, Leigh-on-Sea · £12 per person

Every story links to the original reporting. More all day at theseax.com.

item.title: Essex at 7, Friday 6 November: Essex police commissioner vows to fight plan that could fold Essex Police into a regional super force
item.description: The Seax morning briefing for Friday 6 November.
item.content:encoded:
Weather

Sunny intervals, high 10°C, low 5°C, 10% chance of rain.

⚠ Met Office yellow warning for fog in force until 11am Saturday 7 November

The stories that matter

Essex police commissioner vows to fight plan that could fold Essex Police into a regional super force

Essex · Roger Hirst says there is no public appetite for change in Essex, as a Government-commissioned review is reported to recommend cutting England's 39 forces to as few as nine.

Essex County Council asks residents to help close a £170m gap in one of its toughest budgets this century

Chelmsford · The county council has opened a month-long consultation on its 2027/28 budget, saying government funding changes will cost it more than £50m a year.

Plans emerge for 1GW solar and battery energy park on the Dengie Peninsula

Bradwell-on-Sea, Dengie & Burnham-on-Crouch · Developer Low Carbon has started the national planning process for a scheme it says could power 250,000 homes, and Maldon District Council has until 24 November to say what studies it needs.

A130 southbound shut all weekend between Howe Green and the Rayleigh Spur for maintenance

Howe Green & Rayleigh · Drivers heading south from Chelmsford towards Basildon and Southend face a signed diversion via the A12 and A127 until early on Monday.

Southend opens final consultation on Local Plan it was ordered to publish by ministers

Southend-on-Sea · Residents have until 21 December to comment on the draft blueprint for homes, jobs and infrastructure, which the city council published only after the housing minister intervened.

More than 50,000 still waiting at Southend Hospital as trust backlog falls by 14,000

Southend-on-Sea · Hospital chief executive Fiona Ryan told councillors there is still a long way to go, although waiting lists across the Mid and South Essex trust are starting to come down.

New website launched for 7,750-home Tendring Colchester Borders Garden Community

Colchester & Tendring borders · Three councils have opened a single online hub for the planned new town east of Colchester, with a decision on its planning application expected in summer 2027.

Travel

  • A130 southbound closed between Howe Green Interchange and Rayleigh Spur from 8pm Fri 6 Nov to about 6am Mon 9 Nov; diversion via A12 and A127 at Gallows Corner
  • c2c: no trains at Dagenham Dock, Rainham or Purfleet until at least end of Tue 10 Nov; shuttle buses Upminster to Grays about every 30 min, extra Pitsea to Grays buses 06:50 to 09:30
